questions.text: मानव की द्वितीयक शुक्राणु कोशिका में उपस्थित अलिंगी गुणसूत्रों की संख्या है
questions.text_english: The number of autosomes present in a human secondary spermatocyte
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 22. A human primary spermatocyte (2n = 46) undergoes meiosis I to produce secondary spermatocytes. After meiosis I, each secondary spermatocyte is haploid (n = 23), containing 22 autosomes and 1 sex chromosome. Options A (44) and D (46) correspond to diploid counts, and option C (23) refers to the total chromosome number, not just autosomes.

questions.text: एक एकबीजपत्री बीज (दाने) की अनुप्रस्थ-काट का आरेख नीचे दिया गया है, जिसके भाग-I, II तथा III को नामांकित किया गया है। उस विकल्प का चयन कीजिए जिसमें I, II तथा III भागों को सही अनुक्रम में दर्शाया गया है।
questions.text_english: Given below is a diagram of T.S. of a monocot seed with parts I, II & III labelled. Choose the option where parts I, II and III are identified correctly.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Pericarp, Endosperm, Coleorhiza. In a monocot seed such as maize, Part I (outermost layer) is the Pericarp (fruit wall fused with seed coat), Part II (large central region) is the Endosperm (food storage tissue), and Part III (pointed tip at base) is the Coleorhiza (sheath covering the radicle). Scutellum is the single cotyledon that lies between the endosperm and embryo, not visible as a labelled part in the positions described.

questions.text: सुकेन्द्रकी अनुलेखन के दौरान बनने वाले विषमांगी आरएनए को निम्न प्रकार से आरेखित किया गया है। विषमांगी केन्द्रकीय आरएनए (hnRNA) में उपस्थित इंट्रॉनों तथा एक्ज़ॉनों की संख्या क्रमशः है:
questions.text_english: Given below is a heterogeneous RNA formed during Eukaryotic transcription. How many introns and exons respectively are present in the hnRNA?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 7, 8. In the hnRNA diagram shown, the loops represent introns (non-coding intervening sequences) and the straight segments represent exons (expressed sequences). By counting the loops (introns) = 7 and the straight line segments (exons) = 8. Exons are always one more than introns because exons flank the introns on both sides. Options A, B, and C give incorrect counts that do not match the pattern shown in the diagram.
questions.topic: Transcription in eukaryotes, hnRNA, introns and exons

questions.text: यदि मेसेलसन तथा स्टाल के प्रयोग को 80 मिनट तक (तीसरी पीढ़ी) जारी रखा जाए तो संवर्धन में N¹⁵/N¹⁵ : N¹⁵/N¹⁴ : N¹⁴/N¹⁴ युक्त डीएनए का अनुपात क्या होगा?
questions.text_english: If Meselson and Stahl's experiment is continued for 80 minutes (till III generation) then what would be the ratio of DNA containing N¹⁵/N¹⁵ : N¹⁵/N¹⁴ : N¹⁴/N¹⁴ in the medium?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 0 : 1 : 3. Meselson and Stahl's experiment demonstrated semi-conservative DNA replication. Starting with all-heavy (N15/N15) DNA and shifting to N14 medium: after generation I (20 min), all 2 molecules are hybrid (N15/N14). After generation II (40 min), 2 hybrid and 2 light (N14/N14) molecules form. After generation III (80 min), 8 total molecules exist: 2 hybrid (N15/N14) and 6 light (N14/N14), giving ratio 0 : 2 : 6 = 0 : 1 : 3. No pure heavy (N15/N15) DNA remains after generation I.
questions.topic: Meselson and Stahl experiment, Semi-conservative replication

questions.text: एक बच्चे का रुधिर वर्ग-A है; उसके पिता का रुधिर वर्ग-B तथा माता का रुधिर वर्ग AB है। उस विकल्प को चुनिए जिसमें पिता, माँ (माता) तथा बच्चे के जीनप्ररूप को सही क्रम में दिया गया है:
questions.text_english: A child with blood group A has father with blood group B and the mother with blood group AB. Choose the option that gives the correct genotypes of father, mother and the child:

options.A: Father: Iᴪ i, Mother: Iᴮ i, Child: Iᴪ i
options.B: Father: Iᴪ Iᴮ, Mother: Iᴪ i, Child: Iᴪ Iᴪ
options.C: Father: Iᴮ i, Mother: Iᴪ Iᴮ, Child: Iᴪ i
options.D: Father: Iᴮ Iᴮ, Mother: Iᴪ Iᴮ, Child: Iᴪ Iᴪ

options_english.A: Father: Iᴪ i, Mother: Iᴮ i, Child: Iᴪ i
options_english.B: Father: Iᴪ Iᴮ, Mother: Iᴪ i, Child: Iᴪ Iᴪ
options_english.C: Father: Iᴮ i, Mother: Iᴪ Iᴮ, Child: Iᴪ i
options_english.D: Father: Iᴮ Iᴮ, Mother: Iᴪ Iᴮ, Child: Iᴪ Iᴪ

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Father: Iᴮ i, Mother: Iᴪ Iᴮ, Child: Iᴪ i. The mother has blood group AB, so her genotype must be Iᴪ Iᴮ. The father has blood group B; for the child to have blood group A (genotype Iᴪ i), the child must receive the 'i' allele from the father, so the father's genotype must be Iᴮ i. The child receives Iᴪ from the mother and 'i' from the father, giving genotype Iᴪ i (blood group A). All other options contain genotypic inconsistencies with the stated blood groups.
questions.topic: ABO blood groups, codominance, multiple alleles

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा विकल्प दिए गए पौधों के विकास का सही अनुक्रम दर्शाता है? (i) फर्न (ii) जिन्को (iii) जोस्टेरोफिलम (iv) नीटेल्स
questions.text_english: Which one of the following options shows the correct evolutionary order of the plants mentioned below? (i) Ferns (ii) Ginkgo (iii) Zosterophyllum (iv) Gnetales
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Zosterophyllum → Ferns → Ginkgo → Gnetales. Zosterophyllum is among the earliest vascular plants from the Silurian/Devonian period; Ferns evolved in the Devonian and flourished in the Carboniferous; Ginkgo is a gymnosperm that appeared in the Permian; Gnetales are advanced gymnosperms appearing later. This sequence correctly reflects the evolutionary progression from primitive vascular plants to advanced gymnosperms.
questions.topic: Evolution of plants, Pteridophytes and Gymnosperms

questions.text: कॉलम-I तथा कॉलम-II में दी गई मदों का अध्ययन कीजिए। कॉलम-I की मदों का कॉलम-II की मदों के साथ सही मिलान वाले विकल्प को चुनिए: कॉलम-I: (a) आरएनए पॉलीमरेज-I, (b) आरएनए पॉलीमरेज-II, (c) आरएनए पॉलीमरेज-III | कॉलम-II: (i) 18s आरआरएनए (rRNA), (ii) एसएन आरएनएज (SnRNAs), (iii) hn आरएनए (hnRNA)
questions.text_english: Study the items of Column-I and those of Column-II. Choose the option that correctly matches the items of Column-I with those of Column-II: Column-I: (a) RNA polymerase I, (b) RNA polymerase II, (c) RNA polymerase III | Column-II: (i) 18s rRNA, (ii) SnRNAs, (iii) hnRNA
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) RNA polymerase I → 18s rRNA, RNA polymerase II → hnRNA, RNA polymerase III → SnRNAs. In eukaryotes, RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNA genes (including 18s rRNA); RNA polymerase II transcribes the hnRNA (precursor mRNA); and RNA polymerase III transcribes small nuclear RNAs (SnRNAs) and tRNAs. Option A is incorrect because RNA pol II makes hnRNA, not SnRNA.

questions.text: एक वंशावली विश्लेषण चार्ट में '○═□' निरूपित करता है:
questions.text_english: In a pedigree chart '○═□' represents:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) mating between relatives (consanguineous mating). In a standard pedigree chart, a double horizontal line (○═□) connecting a circle (female) and a square (male) represents consanguineous mating, i.e., mating between blood relatives. A single horizontal line represents unrelated mating. Affected individuals are shown by filled symbols, and non-identical twins are shown by separate convergent lines from a common point.

questions.text: एक गर्भस्थ शिशु (भ्रूण) को अपरा (प्लैसेंटा) के माध्यम से अपनी सगर्भा माँ से कुछ प्रतिरक्षी प्राप्त हुए। भ्रूण (गर्भस्थ शिशु) में विकसित होने वाली प्रतिरक्षा के प्रकार को दर्शाने वाले सही विकल्प को चुनिए।
questions.text_english: The foetus receives some antibodies from their mother through the placenta during pregnancy. Choose the correct option that shows the type of immunity developed in the foetus.

options.A: प्राकृतिक रूप से उपार्जित सक्रिय प्रतिरक्षा
options.B: कृत्रिम रूप से उपार्जित निष्क्रिय प्रतिरक्षा
options.C: प्राकृतिक रूप से उपार्जित निष्क्रिय प्रतिरक्षा
options.D: कृत्रिम रूप से उपार्जित सक्रिय प्रतिरक्षा

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Naturally acquired passive immunity. The foetus receives ready-made antibodies (IgG) from its mother via the placenta without having to mount an immune response of its own. Since no antigen exposure is involved, it is passive immunity. Since it occurs naturally (not through injection), it is naturally acquired. This also explains why newborns have some protection against infections in early life.

questions.text: एक द्विगुणित जीव तीन विस्थलों पर विषमयुग्मजी है, वह जीव कितने प्रकार के युग्मक उत्पन्न कर सकता है?
questions.text_english: A diploid organism is heterozygous for three loci, how many types of gametes can be produced by that organism?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 8. The number of gamete types produced by an organism heterozygous at 'n' loci is 2ⁿ. Here, n = 3 (three heterozygous loci), so 2³ = 8 types of gametes. For example, an organism with genotype AaBbCc produces gametes: ABC, ABc, AbC, Abc, aBC, aBc, abC, abc — 8 types in total. Options A, C, and D correspond to n = 2, 4, and 5 respectively.
questions.topic: Law of independent assortment, gamete types

questions.text: जेल वैद्युत कण-संचलन (इलेक्ट्रॉफोरेसिस) के दौरान डीएनए खंडों के गति करने (दूर जाने) के कारण वे ऐगारोज जेल पर अलग (पृथक) हो जाते हैं। सही विकल्प चुनिए:
questions.text_english: During gel electrophoresis migration of DNA fragments leading to their separation takes place on the agarose gel. Choose the correct option:

options.A: खंड जितने छोटे आकार के होंगे, वे उतनी अधिक दूर जाएँगी।
options.B: धनात्मक आवेशित खंड दूर वाले सिरे की ओर गति करते हैं।
options.C: खंड जितना बड़े आकार का होगा, वे उतनी ही दूर जाएगा।
options.D: ऋणात्मक आवेशित खंड गति नहीं करते।

options_english.A: The smaller the fragment size, the farther it moves.
options_english.B: Positively charged fragments moves to farther end.
options_english.C: The larger the fragment size, the farther it moves.
options_english.D: The negatively charged fragments do not move.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) The smaller the fragment size, the farther it moves. In agarose gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments are negatively charged (due to phosphate groups) and move towards the positive electrode (anode). Smaller fragments experience less resistance from the gel matrix and thus migrate farther. Larger fragments move slower and remain closer to the well. Options B and D are factually incorrect; DNA is negatively charged and does move. Option C is the opposite of the correct principle.

questions.text: उस जीव को पहचानिए जिसके उत्पाद का उपयोग व्यापारिक स्तर पर रक्त-कोलेस्टेरोल को कम करने वाले कारक के रूप में किया जाता है।
questions.text_english: Identify the organism whose product has been commercialised as blood cholesterol lowering agent.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Monascus purpureus. This yeast produces statins, specifically lovastatin (Monacolin K), which are commercialised as blood cholesterol-lowering agents (statins). Trichoderma polysporum produces cyclosporin A (an immunosuppressant). Saccharomyces cerevisiae is used in fermentation and bread making. Aspergillus niger is used for citric acid production.
questions.topic: Microbes in production of bioactive molecules

questions.text: अभिकथन (A): 'XX-XY' प्रकार की लिंग-निर्धारण क्रियाविधि नर विषमयुग्मकता (हिटिरोगेमिटी) का उदाहरण है। कारण (R): पक्षियों में नर दो प्रकार के युग्मक उत्पन्न करते हैं, अतः उनमें नर विषमयुग्मकता प्रेक्षित होती है।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): 'XX – XY' type of sex-determination mechanism is an example of male heterogamety. Reason (R): In birds male heterogamety is observed as males produce two different types of gametes.
questions.instruction_line: प्रश्न संख्या 13 से 16 में दो कथन – अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दिए गए हैं। इन प्रश्नों के उत्तर नीचे दिए अनुसार उचित विकल्प को चुनकर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Question number 13 to 16 consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). (B) Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A). (C) (A) is true, but (R) is false. (D) (A) is false, but (R) is true.

options.A: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या हो रही है।
options.B: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं हो रही है।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false. The Assertion is correct: in XX-XY type sex determination (as in humans), males are XY and produce two types of gametes (X-bearing and Y-bearing), making males heterogametic. However, the Reason is false: in birds, it is the FEMALE that is heterogametic (ZW), not the male. Bird males are ZZ (homogametic) and produce only one type of gamete. So the reason incorrectly states that bird males show heterogamety.

questions.text: अभिकथन (A): इंग्लैंड में औद्योगिकरण के पश्चात् श्वेत पंखी शलभों की संख्या कम हो गई। कारण (R): इंग्लैंड के ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में औद्योगिकरण का प्रभाव अधिक देखा गया।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): The number of white winged moths decreased after industrialisation in England. Reason (R): Effects of industrialisation were more marked in rural areas of England.

options.A: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या हो रही है।
options.B: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं हो रही है।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false. The Assertion is true: industrialisation in England led to soot-covered dark tree trunks, making white-winged moths (Biston betularia) more visible to predators, thus reducing their numbers (industrial melanism). However, the Reason is false: the effects of industrialisation were more marked in industrial/urban areas, not in rural areas. In rural (non-industrial) areas, tree trunks remained light-coloured, so white moths continued to survive better there.

questions.text: अभिकथन (A): द्वितीयक प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया प्राथमिक प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया की अपेक्षा तीव्रतर तथा दृढ़तर होती है। कारण (R): संभवतः हमारे शरीर को प्रथम मुठभेड़ की स्मृति रहती है, अतः उसी रोगकारक से पुनः मुठभेड़ (सामना) होने पर उच्च तीव्रता की द्रुतगामी अनुक्रिया होती है।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): Secondary immune response is quicker and stronger than the primary immune response. Reason (R): Our body appears to have the memory of the first encounter therefore response to the subsequent encounter with the same pathogen is quick.

options.A: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या हो रही है।
options.B: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं हो रही है।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. The secondary immune response is indeed quicker and produces higher levels of antibodies compared to the primary response. This is because memory B and T cells are generated during the first encounter (primary response). Upon re-exposure to the same antigen, these memory cells rapidly proliferate and differentiate, producing a faster and stronger response. Thus, the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

questions.text: अभिकथन (A): एडीए की कमी (अभाव/हीनता) वाले रोगी को नियत सामयिक अंतराल पर आनुवंशिकतः निर्मित लसीकाणुओं के निवेशन की आवश्यकता होती है। कारण (R): लसीकाणु अमर नहीं हैं, उनकी जीवन अवधि भी निश्चित है।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): A patient of ADA-deficiency requires periodic or repeated infusion of genetically-engineered lymphocytes. Reason (R): Lymphocytes are not immortal, but have life span.

options.A: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या हो रही है।
options.B: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं हो रही है।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. ADA (Adenosine Deaminase) deficiency is a form of SCID. In gene therapy, functional ADA genes are introduced into the patient's lymphocytes outside the body. However, since lymphocytes are not immortal and have a finite lifespan, these engineered cells eventually die. Therefore, the patient requires periodic infusions of freshly engineered lymphocytes to maintain the therapeutic effect. The Reason correctly explains the need for repeated infusion stated in the Assertion.

questions.text: परीक्षार्थी विकल्प (A) अथवा (B) में से किसी एक का उत्तर लिखें।
questions.text_english: Student to attempt either option (A) or (B).
questions.instruction_line: विकल्प (A) अथवा (B) में से किसी एक का उत्तर लिखें।

sub_questions.text: (A) (i) चित्र में नामांकित 'P' तथा 'Q' की पहचान कीजिए। (ii) चित्र में अंकित 'P' तथा 'Q' हॉर्मोन के स्रोत निर्दिष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (A) (i) Identify 'P' and 'Q' labelled in the diagram. (ii) Specify the source of the hormone 'P' and 'Q' marked in the diagram. [Diagram shows ovarian hormone levels over a menstrual cycle with P and Q labelled]

key_points: P is Oestrogen (Estrogen); Q is Progesterone
P (Oestrogen) is secreted by the Graafian follicle (growing follicle) of the ovary
Q (Progesterone) is secreted by the Corpus luteum formed after ovulation

sub_questions.solution: In the diagram showing ovarian hormone levels across the menstrual cycle, P represents Oestrogen (Estrogen), which peaks just before ovulation around day 13-14. Q represents Progesterone, which rises after ovulation and peaks around days 21-22. Oestrogen (P) is secreted by the Graafian follicle (developing follicle) present in the ovary during the follicular phase. Progesterone (Q) is secreted by the Corpus luteum, a temporary endocrine structure that forms from the ruptured Graafian follicle after ovulation during the luteal phase.

sub_questions.text: (B) (i) चित्र में नामांकित 'P' तथा 'Q' को पहचानिए। (ii) नर (पुरुष) तथा स्त्री दोनों में हॉर्मोन 'P' की भूमिका का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (B) (i) Identify 'P' and 'Q' labelled in the above diagram. (ii) Write down the role of hormone 'P' in both males and females. [Diagram shows pituitary hormone levels over the menstrual cycle with P and Q labelled]

key_points: P is LH (Luteinising Hormone); Q is FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone)
Role of LH in females: triggers ovulation (LH surge), stimulates formation of corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone
Role of LH in males: stimulates Leydig cells (interstitial cells) in the testes to produce testosterone

sub_questions.solution: In the pituitary hormone level diagram, P represents LH (Luteinising Hormone), which shows a sharp surge around day 14 triggering ovulation. Q represents FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone). In females, LH (P) causes ovulation by triggering the rupture of the mature Graafian follicle, and then stimulates the formation of the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone to maintain the uterine lining. In males, LH acts on the Leydig cells (interstitial cells) of the testes and stimulates them to secrete the male sex hormone testosterone, which is essential for spermatogenesis and development of secondary sexual characters.

sub_questions.text: (a) α-थैलेसीमिया रोग का नियंत्रण करने वाले दो सन्निकट लग्न जीनों के नाम लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Write two closely linked genes that control alpha-thalassemia.

key_points: HBA1 and HBA2 (alpha globin genes on chromosome 16)

sub_questions.solution: The two closely linked genes that control alpha-thalassemia are HBA1 and HBA2. Both are located on chromosome 16 and encode the alpha-globin chains of haemoglobin. Deletions or mutations in these genes reduce or eliminate alpha-globin production, leading to alpha-thalassemia.

sub_questions.text: (b) हीमोग्लोबिन के ग्लोबिन अणु पर थैलेसीमिया तथा दात्रकोशिका अरक्तता के प्रभाव के आधार पर इन रोगों के बीच अंतर स्थापित कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Differentiate between thalassemia and sickle cell anaemia on the basis of their effect on globin molecule of Haemoglobin.

key_points: Thalassemia: quantitative defect – reduced or absent synthesis of globin chains
Sickle cell anaemia: qualitative defect – abnormal structure of beta-globin chain due to point mutation (glutamic acid replaced by valine at position 6)

sub_questions.solution: Thalassemia is a quantitative disorder of haemoglobin in which there is reduced or absent synthesis of one of the globin chains (alpha or beta). The globin chains produced are structurally normal but their quantity is insufficient. Sickle cell anaemia, on the other hand, is a qualitative disorder in which the beta-globin chain has an abnormal structure due to a point mutation — glutamic acid is replaced by valine at position 6. This causes the haemoglobin (HbS) to polymerise under low oxygen conditions, making red blood cells sickle-shaped.

questions.instruction_line: विकल्प (A) अथवा (B) में से किसी एक का उत्तर लिखें।

sub_questions.text: (A) ऐसी किन्हीं दो परिस्थितियों का वर्णन कीजिए जिनमें एक चिकित्सक (डॉक्टर) पूर्वनिर्मित प्रतिरक्षियों (प्रतिआविष) को रोगी व्यक्ति के शरीर में निवेशित करने की सलाह देते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: (A) Describe any two situations where a medical doctor would recommend injection of a pre-formed antibodies (antitoxins) into the body of a patient.

key_points: Snake bite – anti-snake venom (antitoxin) is injected for immediate passive immunity
Tetanus – tetanus antitoxin (TIG) is injected when a patient has a deep wound and needs immediate protection

sub_questions.solution: A doctor recommends injection of pre-formed antibodies (antitoxins) when the patient needs immediate protection and there is no time for the immune system to generate its own response. The first situation is a snake bite, where anti-venom containing pre-formed antibodies against snake toxins is injected to neutralise the venom quickly. The second situation is a patient with a deep, dirty wound susceptible to tetanus; the doctor injects tetanus immunoglobulin (antitoxin) for immediate passive immunity, especially when the patient has not been previously vaccinated.

sub_questions.text: (B) संक्रमित मादा ऐनोफेलीज़ मच्छर के काटने के परिणामस्वरूप मलेरिया रोग के बीजाणुओं (स्पोरोज़ॉइट्स) के मानव शरीर में प्रविष्ट होने के तुरंत बाद मलेरिया के अभिलक्षण परिलक्षित नहीं होते हैं। व्याख्या कीजिए कि ऐसा क्यों होता है।
sub_questions.text_english: (B) The symptoms of malaria do not appear immediately after the entry of sporozoites into the human body when bitten by female Anopheles mosquito. Explain why it happens.

key_points: Sporozoites first enter liver cells and multiply (exo-erythrocytic cycle) – this is asymptomatic
Symptoms appear only when parasites enter red blood cells, multiply, burst them, and release toxins – the erythrocytic cycle causes fever and chills

sub_questions.solution: After the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito, sporozoites enter the bloodstream and travel to the liver, where they infect hepatocytes (liver cells) and undergo multiple rounds of multiplication. This exo-erythrocytic (pre-erythrocytic) phase is completely asymptomatic. Only after this incubation period do the parasites (merozoites) enter the red blood cells and begin the erythrocytic cycle. The rupture of red blood cells and release of haemozoin toxin causes the characteristic symptoms of fever, chills, and anaemia. This explains the delay between infection and the appearance of malarial symptoms.

questions.text: निम्न आरेख में एक डीएनए खंड के नाइट्रोजनी क्षारकों के अभिक्रम को प्रदर्शित किया गया है। इसका प्रेक्षण करके संबंधित निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर लिखिए: 5'-CAGAATTCTTA-3' / 3'-GTCTTAAGAAT-5' (a) डीएनए अनुक्रम की पहचान करने वाले प्रतिबंधन एंजाइम का नाम लिखिए। (b) प्रतिबंधन एंजाइम द्वारा पैलींड्रोम को काटने के बाद क्षारकों का अनुक्रम लिखिए। (c) इस प्रक्रम में पाचन के बाद बनने वाले सिरों को 'चिपचिपा छोर' क्यों कहा जाता है?
questions.text_english: Observe the given sequence of nitrogenous bases on a DNA fragment and answer the following questions: 5'-C A G A A T T C T T A-3' / 3'-G T C T T A A G A A T-5' (a) Name the restriction enzyme which can recognise the DNA sequence. (b) Write the sequence after restriction enzyme cut the palindrome. (c) Why are the ends generated after digestion called 'Sticky Ends'?

key_points: (a) EcoRI recognises the palindromic sequence GAATTC
(b) After EcoRI cuts: 5'-CAGAATTC cuts to 5'-CAG and AATTCTTA-3'; producing 5' overhangs
(c) Single-stranded complementary overhangs can form hydrogen bonds with complementary sticky ends on other DNA fragments, hence called sticky ends

questions.solution:
(a) The restriction enzyme that recognises this DNA sequence is EcoRI. It recognises the palindromic sequence 5'-GAATTC-3' present within the given DNA fragment.

(b) EcoRI cuts the palindrome between G and AATTC on both strands. After cutting, the resulting fragments are:
5'-CAG     AATTCTTA-3'
3'-GTCTTAA     GAAT-5'
This produces single-stranded 5' overhangs: 5'-AATT-3' on each fragment.

(c) The ends are called 'Sticky Ends' because the single-stranded overhang sequences (5'-AATT-3') are complementary to each other. These unpaired bases can form hydrogen bonds with complementary sticky ends of other DNA molecules cut by the same enzyme, allowing different DNA fragments to join together. This property is used in recombinant DNA technology for inserting a gene into a vector.
questions.topic: Restriction enzymes, Palindromic sequences, Sticky ends

sub_questions.text: (A) पादप प्लवकों से प्रारंभ करते हुए तीन पोषण स्तरों वाला जैव मात्रा (भार) का पिरैमिड बनाइए। क्या यह पिरैमिड खड़ा है अथवा उलटा? अपने उत्तर की न्यायसंगतता सिद्ध कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (A) Construct a pyramid of biomass starting with phytoplankton, label its three trophic levels. Is the pyramid upright or inverted? Justify your answer.

key_points: Pyramid: Phytoplankton (Producers) at base → Zooplankton (Primary consumers) → Fish (Secondary consumers) at top
The pyramid of biomass starting with phytoplankton in aquatic ecosystems is INVERTED
Justification: Phytoplankton reproduce very rapidly and have a very short lifespan, so at any given time their biomass is less than that of the zooplankton that feed on them

sub_questions.solution: The pyramid of biomass starting with phytoplankton has three trophic levels: Phytoplankton (Producers) at the base, Zooplankton (Primary consumers) in the middle, and Fish (Secondary consumers) at the top. This pyramid is inverted. The justification is that in aquatic ecosystems, phytoplankton have a very rapid rate of reproduction and a very short lifespan. At any given moment, the standing crop (biomass) of phytoplankton is less than that of zooplankton. Hence the base (producers) has less biomass than the consumers, resulting in an inverted pyramid.

sub_questions.text: (B) एक ऐसे पारिस्थितिक तंत्र की संख्या का पिरैमिड बनाइए जिसमें कीटों की बड़ी समष्टि एक बड़े वृक्ष पर आश्रित है। यह कीट छोटे पक्षियों द्वारा खाए जाते हैं; जो आगे (पुनः) बड़े पक्षियों द्वारा खाए जाते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: (B) Draw a pyramid of number where a large population of insects feed upon a very big tree. The insects in turn, are eaten by small birds which in turn are fed upon by big birds.

key_points: Tree (1) at base → Insects (many thousands) → Small birds → Big birds at top
This pyramid of numbers is inverted (spindle-shaped) because a single tree supports a very large number of insects

sub_questions.solution: The pyramid of numbers for this ecosystem is inverted (spindle-shaped). At the base is a single large tree (producer, number = 1). A large population of insects (primary consumers, numbering in thousands) feeds on this tree. The insects are eaten by small birds (secondary consumers, fewer in number), which are in turn eaten by big birds (tertiary consumers, fewest in number) at the apex. Since the number of producers (1 tree) is far less than the number of consumers (insects), the base is narrower than the middle trophic level, making the overall pyramid inverted.

sub_questions.text: (a) एक द्विकोष्ठी परागकोश की प्रत्येक लघुबीजाणुधानी में 200 लघुबीजाणु मातृ कोशिकाएँ हैं। इस परागकोश से कितने नरयुग्मकोद्भिद् उत्पन्न (निर्मित) होंगे?
sub_questions.text_english: (a) A bilobed dithecous anther has 200 microspore mother cells per microsporangium. How many male gametophytes can be produced by this anther?

key_points: Each microsporangium has 200 MMCs, each producing 4 microspores by meiosis = 800 microspores per microsporangium
A dithecous (bilobed) anther has 2 lobes, each with 2 microsporangia = 4 microsporangia total
Total microspores = 4 × 800 = 3200; each microspore develops into 1 male gametophyte (pollen grain)
Total male gametophytes = 3200

sub_questions.solution: A bilobed dithecous anther has 2 lobes, each lobe containing 2 microsporangia, giving a total of 4 microsporangia per anther. Each microsporangium contains 200 microspore mother cells (MMCs). Each MMC undergoes meiosis to produce 4 microspores. Therefore, each microsporangium produces 200 × 4 = 800 microspores. The total microspores from 4 microsporangia = 4 × 800 = 3200. Since each microspore develops into one male gametophyte (pollen grain), the total number of male gametophytes produced by this anther is 3200.

sub_questions.text: (b) एक परागकण के बाह्य-चोल तथा अंतः-चोल परतों के संगठन (संरचना) का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Write the composition of intine and exine layers of a pollen grain.

key_points: Exine (outer wall): made of sporopollenin, a highly resistant organic polymer; has apertures called germ pores
Intine (inner wall): made of cellulose and pectin; thin and continuous

sub_questions.solution: A pollen grain has two layers: the outer exine and the inner intine. The exine is the outer, hard, and highly resistant layer made of sporopollenin, which is one of the most resistant biological substances known. It can withstand high temperatures, strong acids, and alkalis. The exine has special apertures called germ pores through which the pollen tube emerges. The intine is the inner, thin, and delicate layer made of cellulose and pectin. It is continuous and not interrupted by germ pores.

sub_questions.text: (a) सहायक जनन प्रौद्योगिकी के विभिन्न तरीकों के संक्षिप्त रूप (संकेताक्षर) निम्नलिखित हैं, इनके पूरे नाम लिखिए: (i) जेडआईएफटी (ZIFT), (ii) आईसीएसआई (ICSI), (iii) आईयूटी (IUT), (iv) जीआईएफटी (GIFT)
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Abbreviations used for the different modes of assisted reproductive technology are given below. Expand the abbreviations: (i) ZIFT, (ii) ICSI, (iii) IUT, (iv) GIFT

key_points: (i) ZIFT = Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer
(ii) ICSI = Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection
(iii) IUT = Intra Uterine Transfer
(iv) GIFT = Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer

sub_questions.solution: The full forms of the ART abbreviations are: (i) ZIFT stands for Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer, in which a zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) is transferred into the fallopian tube. (ii) ICSI stands for Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection, in which a sperm is directly injected into the ovum in the laboratory. (iii) IUT stands for Intra Uterine Transfer, in which an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres is transferred into the uterus. (iv) GIFT stands for Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer, in which an ovum collected from a donor is transferred into the fallopian tube of a woman who cannot produce eggs.

sub_questions.text: (b) उल्ववेधन (एम्नियोसेंटेसिस) पर वैधानिक प्रतिबंध क्यों है? कम से कम दो कारण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Why is there a statutory ban on Amniocentesis? Give at least two reasons.

key_points: Amniocentesis is misused for sex determination of the foetus, leading to female foeticide
It leads to selective abortion of female foetuses, causing an imbalanced sex ratio in society

sub_questions.solution: Amniocentesis, a procedure in which amniotic fluid is sampled to study foetal chromosomes, has been legally banned in India (under PNDT Act) due to its widespread misuse. First, the technique was commonly used for prenatal sex determination, revealing whether the foetus is male or female. Second, based on this information, many female foetuses were selectively aborted, leading to a severely skewed and declining sex ratio in the population. The government imposed a statutory ban to prevent this misuse, protect the female child, and maintain a healthy sex ratio in society.

questions.text: एक अलिंगी दृश्यप्ररूपी अभिलक्षण के लिए एक विस्थल पर स्थित लक्षण (विशेषक) के लिए एक समयुग्मजी (होमोजाइगस) मादा तथा एक विषमयुग्मजी नर के बीच संकरण (क्रॉस) से प्राप्त प्रथम पीढ़ी (F₁) संतति के लक्षण वितरण को पनेट वर्ग की सहायता से समझाइए।
questions.text_english: Using a Punnett square workout the distribution of an autosomal phenotypic feature in the first filial generation after a cross between a homozygous female and a heterozygous male for a single locus.

key_points: Homozygous female: AA; Heterozygous male: Aa
Punnett square gives F1: AA : Aa = 1:1
Phenotypic ratio: 100% show dominant phenotype (all offspring express the dominant trait)

questions.solution:
Let the autosomal trait be controlled by alleles A (dominant) and a (recessive). The homozygous female has genotype AA and the heterozygous male has genotype Aa.

Punnett Square:

        A (female)    A (female)
A (male)    AA            AA
a (male)    Aa            Aa

The F1 generation consists of 2 AA : 2 Aa = 1 AA : 1 Aa. All four offspring (2 AA and 2 Aa) express the dominant phenotype. Therefore, the phenotypic ratio in the F1 generation is 100% dominant phenotype (all individuals show the dominant trait). There is no individual showing the recessive phenotype in this cross.

questions.text: प्राकृतिक वरण हार्डी-विनबर्ग संतुलन को किस प्रकार प्रभावित करता है? ग्राफ की सहायता से इसकी व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: How does the process of Natural Selection affect Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium? Explain with the help of graphs.

key_points: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium states allele and genotype frequencies remain constant in a population if no evolution is occurring
Natural selection acts as an agent of evolution that disturbs H-W equilibrium by favouring certain alleles over others
The selected allele increases in frequency over generations while the other decreases

questions.solution: The Hardy-Weinberg principle states that allele frequencies in a population remain constant from generation to generation if no evolutionary forces act upon it. The conditions for equilibrium include no mutation, random mating, no natural selection, no genetic drift, and no gene flow. Natural selection is one of the major disturbing forces that violates H-W equilibrium. When natural selection acts on a population, it favours individuals with certain beneficial alleles, increasing their reproductive success. Over successive generations, the frequency of the favoured allele (for example, allele A) increases in the gene pool while the disfavoured allele (a) decreases. On a graph, if allele frequency (p) is plotted against time (generations), the curve for the selected allele shows a progressive increase (sigmoid or directional rise) while the other allele declines. This shift in allele frequency constitutes microevolution, which breaks the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. Thus, natural selection drives directional change in allele frequencies and is a primary mechanism of evolution.

questions.text: किसी भी खेल प्रतिस्पर्धा के आयोजन से पूर्व ड्रग के परीक्षण हेतु खिलाड़ियों के रुधिर तथा मूत्र के नमूने लिए जाते हैं। (a) इस प्रकार के परीक्षण क्यों किए जाते हैं? (b) आयोजक सामान्यतः जिन ड्रगों के लिए परीक्षण करते हैं उनके नाम लिखिए। (c) दो पौधों के वैज्ञानिक नाम लिखिए जिनसे इन ड्रगों को प्राप्त किया जाता है।
questions.text_english: Samples of blood and urine of a sportsperson are collected before any sports event for drug tests. (a) Why there is a need to conduct such tests? (b) Name the drugs the authorities usually look for. (c) Write the generic names of two plants from which these drugs are obtained.

key_points: (a) To detect the use of performance-enhancing drugs (doping) that give an unfair advantage and harm health
(b) Cannabinoids, cocaine, narcotics, anabolic steroids
(c) Cannabis sativa (source of cannabinoids/marijuana) and Erythroxylum coca (source of cocaine)

questions.solution:
(a) Drug tests are conducted on sportspersons before competitions to detect the use of performance-enhancing drugs, commonly called doping. Such substances artificially enhance muscle strength, endurance, and aggression, giving an unfair advantage to the user over other competitors. These drugs also cause serious short-term and long-term health hazards. The tests ensure fair competition and protect the health of athletes.

(b) The drugs that authorities usually test for include cannabinoids (marijuana, hashish), cocaine, narcotics (morphine, heroin), and anabolic steroids. These are psychotropic substances that affect the central nervous system or enhance performance.

(c) Two plants from which these drugs are obtained are: (i) Cannabis sativa – source of cannabinoids such as marijuana, hashish, and charas, obtained from its flowers, leaves, and resin; (ii) Erythroxylum coca – source of cocaine (coke), a powerful stimulant that interferes with dopamine transport in the brain.

sub_questions.text: (a) हमारे शरीर में संश्लेषित इंसुलिन, एली लिली नामक कंपनी द्वारा पुनयोगज डीएनए तकनीक का उपयोग करके संश्लेषित इंसुलिन से किस प्रकार भिन्न है? दोनों के बीच विभेदन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) The insulin synthesised in our body is different from that synthesised by Eli Lilly company using recombinant DNA technology. Differentiate between them.

key_points: Natural insulin (in body): produced as proinsulin with A, B chains and C peptide; C peptide is removed post-translationally to give active insulin
Recombinant insulin (Eli Lilly): produced as separate A and B chains in E. coli, then combined by disulfide bonds; lacks C peptide; called Humulin

sub_questions.solution: The insulin synthesised naturally in our body is initially produced as an inactive precursor called proinsulin. Proinsulin consists of three polypeptide chains: the A chain, the B chain, and a connecting C peptide. The C peptide is enzymatically removed post-translationally in the Golgi apparatus, yielding mature active insulin with only A and B chains linked by disulfide bonds. In contrast, the recombinant insulin produced by Eli Lilly (called Humulin) is manufactured using recombinant DNA technology. The A and B chain genes are separately cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli bacteria. The chains are then extracted and combined in vitro by creating disulfide bonds to form active insulin. This recombinant insulin does not contain the C peptide and is structurally identical to human insulin.

sub_questions.text: (b) आजकल जन्तु स्रोत से निकषित इंसुलिन का उपयोग क्यों नहीं किया जाता है?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Why the insulin extracted from an animal source is not in use these days?

key_points: Animal insulin (from pig/cow) is slightly different in amino acid sequence from human insulin
It causes allergic reactions / immune response in some diabetic patients

sub_questions.solution: Insulin extracted from animal sources (such as pigs and cattle) was used for many years to treat diabetes. However, it is no longer widely used because animal insulin differs slightly in its amino acid sequence from human insulin. When injected into humans, this minor structural difference can trigger an allergic or immune reaction in some patients. Recombinant human insulin (Humulin) is now preferred because it is identical to human insulin, reduces the risk of immune reactions, and can be produced in large quantities without relying on animal slaughter.

questions.solution: See sub-questions (a) and (b) for complete solutions.

sub_questions.text: (a) एक ऐसी समष्टि के लिए ग्राफीय आरेख बनाइए जो पोषण क्षमता की चरम सीमा तक पहुँच गयी हो।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Draw a graph for a population whose population density has reached the carrying capacity.

key_points: S-shaped (logistic) growth curve where the population rises and then levels off at carrying capacity K

sub_questions.solution: A population that has reached the carrying capacity (K) follows a logistic (S-shaped or sigmoid) growth curve. The graph has population size (N) on the y-axis and time on the x-axis. Initially, growth is slow (lag phase), then accelerates rapidly (log phase), and finally slows down and levels off as the population reaches K (plateau/stationary phase). The curve forms a characteristic S-shape, and the population density stabilises at or near K due to limited resources.

sub_questions.text: (b) दो समष्टि वृद्धि वक्रों में से कौन सा वृद्धि वक्र अधिकतर समष्टियों के लिए अधिक यथार्थ-पूर्ण माना जाता है? क्यों?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Out of the two population growth curves, which one is considered a more realistic for most populations? Why?

key_points: Logistic (S-shaped) growth curve is more realistic
Because no population has unlimited resources; food, space, and other resources are limited in nature

sub_questions.solution: The logistic (S-shaped or sigmoid) growth curve is considered more realistic for most natural populations. This is because in nature, resources such as food, water, shelter, and space are always limited. As the population grows and approaches the carrying capacity (K), competition for resources increases, birth rates fall, and death rates rise, thereby checking unlimited growth. The exponential (J-shaped) growth curve assumes unlimited resources, which is an idealistic condition rarely found in nature. Thus, the logistic model better represents real population dynamics.

sub_questions.text: (c) जिस समष्टि के लिए स्रोत सीमित न (असीमित) हो उसका समष्टि वृद्धि वक्र आरेखित कीजिए तथा इसका समीकरण भी लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (c) Draw a growth curve where resources are not limiting for the growth of a population and give its equation.

key_points: Exponential (J-shaped) growth curve
Equation: dN/dt = rN (where N = population size, r = intrinsic rate of natural increase, t = time)

sub_questions.solution: When resources are not limiting (unlimited food, space, etc.), a population shows exponential growth, represented by a J-shaped curve. On the graph, population size (N) is on the y-axis and time (t) is on the x-axis; the curve rises steeply and continuously with no plateau. The equation for exponential growth is: dN/dt = rN, where dN/dt is the rate of change in population size per unit time, r is the intrinsic rate of natural increase (birth rate – death rate), and N is the current population size. An equivalent form is Nt = N₀ · e^(rt), showing that the population grows without bounds.

questions.text: हमारे शरीर में प्रतिरक्षा दो प्रकार की होती है: (i) सहज प्रतिरक्षा तथा (ii) उपार्जित प्रतिरक्षा। सहज प्रतिरक्षा एक प्रकार का अविशिष्ट रक्षा उपागम है, जबकि उपार्जित प्रतिरक्षा रोगजनक-विशिष्ट है; जिसे विशिष्ट प्रतिरक्षा भी कहा जाता है जिसका अभिलक्षण स्मृति है। प्रतिरक्षी अणु किसी प्रतिजन के प्रति विशिष्ट होते हैं। हमारे शरीर में विभिन्न प्रकार के प्रतिरक्षी अणु निर्मित होते हैं; इनके चार उदाहरण IgA, IgE, IgG तथा IgM हैं। जब हमारा शरीर किसी रोगजनक से पहली बार सामना करता है तो इसे प्राथमिक अनुक्रिया कहते हैं तथा जब पुनः उसी प्रतिजन/रोगजनक से उसका सामना होता है तो उसे द्वितीयक अनुक्रिया कहते हैं।
questions.text_english: Immunity in our body is of two types: (i) Innate immunity and (ii) acquired immunity. Innate immunity is a non-specific defence mechanism, whereas acquired immunity is pathogen-specific; it is called specific immunity too. Acquired immunity is characterised by memory. Antibodies are specific to antigens and there are different types of antibodies produced in our body: they are IgA, IgE, IgG and IgM. It shows primary response when it encounters the pathogen for the first time and secondary response during the subsequent encounters with the same Antigen/Pathogen.

sub_questions.text: (a) दो प्रकार की विशिष्ट कोशिकाओं के नाम लिखिए जो प्राथमिक तथा द्वितीयक प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया को सम्पादित करती हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Name the two types of specialised cells which carry out the primary and secondary immune response.

key_points: B lymphocytes (B cells) and T lymphocytes (T cells)

sub_questions.solution: The two types of specialised cells that carry out the primary and secondary immune responses are B lymphocytes (B cells) and T lymphocytes (T cells). B cells are responsible for humoral (antibody-mediated) immunity and produce antibodies. T cells mediate cell-mediated immunity. Both B and T cells generate memory cells during the primary response, which are responsible for the rapid and stronger secondary response upon re-exposure to the same antigen.

sub_questions.text: (b) प्रतिरक्षी अणु-माध्यित प्रतिरक्षा को तरल प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया (ह्युमोरल इम्यून रेसपांस) भी कहा जाता है, क्यों?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Why is the antibody-mediated immunity also called as humoral immune response?

key_points: Antibodies are present in blood and lymph (body fluids/humour); since they work through body fluids, it is called humoral immunity

sub_questions.solution: Antibody-mediated immunity is called humoral immune response because the antibodies produced by B lymphocytes (plasma cells) are secreted into the blood and lymph — the body fluids. The Latin word 'humor' means fluid. Since the immune response is carried out through antibodies present in body fluids (blood and lymph) rather than through direct cell-to-cell contact, it is termed humoral immunity.

sub_questions.text: (c) यदि समुचित (उपयुक्त) दाता से प्रतिरोपण अंग न प्राप्त किया जाए तो प्रतिरोपण सामान्यतः अस्वीकार (नकार) कर दिए जाते हैं। (i) प्रतिरोप को अस्वीकार करने के लिए हमारे शरीर के प्रतिरक्षा तंत्र में पाये जाने वाले विशिष्ट अभिलक्षण का उल्लेख कीजिए। (ii) इसमें शामिल कोशिकाओं तथा प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया के प्रकार का नाम लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (c) The organ transplants are often rejected if not taken from suitable compatible persons. (i) Mention the characteristic of our immune system that is responsible for the graft rejection. (ii) Name the type of immune response and the cell involved in it.

key_points: (i) The immune system can distinguish self from non-self; it recognises foreign MHC (Major Histocompatibility Complex) antigens on the transplanted organ as non-self
(ii) Cell-mediated immunity; T lymphocytes (cytotoxic T cells) are involved

sub_questions.solution:
(i) The immune system possesses the ability to distinguish between 'self' and 'non-self' tissues. When an organ is transplanted from a non-compatible donor, the immune system recognises the foreign MHC (Major Histocompatibility Complex) proteins, also known as HLA antigens, on the surface of the donor cells as non-self. This recognition triggers the rejection response.

(ii) The type of immune response responsible for graft rejection is cell-mediated immunity (CMI). The cells involved are cytotoxic T lymphocytes (Tc cells or CD8+ T cells), which directly attack and destroy the foreign transplanted cells, leading to rejection of the graft.

sub_questions.text: (d) सक्रिय प्रतिरक्षा निष्क्रिय प्रतिरक्षा से किस प्रकार भिन्न है?
sub_questions.text_english: (d) How is active immunity different from passive immunity?

key_points: Active immunity: body produces its own antibodies in response to antigen exposure; long-lasting; has memory
Passive immunity: ready-made antibodies are transferred into the body; short-lived; no memory

sub_questions.solution: Active immunity develops when the body is exposed to an antigen (through infection or vaccination) and responds by producing its own antibodies and memory cells. This type of immunity is long-lasting and effective upon re-exposure. Passive immunity, on the other hand, involves the transfer of ready-made antibodies produced by another individual or organism into the body. Examples include antibodies transferred from mother to foetus via placenta (natural) or injection of antitoxins/antivenom (artificial). Passive immunity provides immediate protection but is short-lived because no memory cells are produced and the borrowed antibodies degrade over time.

questions.text: डीएनए की एक रज्जुक से आनुवंशिक सूचनाओं का आरएनए में प्रतिलिपीकरण की प्रक्रिया को अनुलेखन कहते हैं। पूरकता का सिद्धांत अनुलेखन प्रक्रम को नियंत्रित करता है सिवाय इसके कि थाइमीन के स्थान पर यूरेसिल क्षारयुग्म बनाता है। निम्न रूप से आरेखित पूर्ण अनुलेखन इकाई का अध्ययन कीजिए तथा उसके आधार पर निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर लिखिए।
questions.text_english: The process of copying the genetic information from one strand of DNA into RNA is termed as transcription. The principle of complementarity of bases governs the process of transcription, also except that uracil comes in place of thymine. Study the complete transcription unit given below and answer the following questions:

sub_questions.text: (a) अनुलेखन प्रक्रम में शामिल प्रमुख एंजाइम का नाम लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Name the main enzyme involved in the process of transcription.

key_points: RNA polymerase

sub_questions.solution: The main enzyme involved in transcription is RNA polymerase. It catalyses the synthesis of RNA from the DNA template strand using the principle of complementarity of bases. In prokaryotes, a single RNA polymerase transcribes all types of RNA, whereas in eukaryotes there are three types (RNA pol I, II, and III) each responsible for transcribing different types of RNA.

sub_questions.text: (b) अनुलेखन इकाई (एकल) में डीएनए के कोडिंग रज्जुक तथा टेम्पलेट रज्जुक को पहचानिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Identify coding strand and template strand of DNA in the transcription unit.

key_points: In the diagram, the strand running 3' to 5' (bottom strand, 5' to 3' going right) with arrow B pointing upward is the template strand
The strand running 5' to 3' (top, 3' to 5' going left) is the coding/non-template strand

sub_questions.solution: In the transcription unit diagram shown, the strand that runs from 3' to 5' direction (towards which RNA polymerase moves) is the template strand (also called antisense strand). RNA polymerase reads this strand in 3' to 5' direction and synthesises the RNA in 5' to 3' direction. The other strand, which has the same base sequence as the RNA (except T in place of U), is the coding strand (also called sense strand or non-template strand), running in the 5' to 3' direction. Based on the diagram provided, the lower strand (with arrow B) represents the template strand and the upper strand represents the coding strand.

sub_questions.text: (c) चित्र में (C) तथा (D) को पहचानिए तथा अनुलेखन प्रक्रम में उनकी सार्थकता (महत्व) का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (c) Identify (C) and (D) in the diagram, mention their significance in the process of transcription.

key_points: C = Promoter region; significance: RNA polymerase binds here to initiate transcription
D = Terminator region; significance: signals the termination/stop of transcription

sub_questions.solution: In the transcription unit diagram, C represents the Promoter region and D represents the Terminator region. The Promoter (C) is a DNA sequence located upstream (at the 3' end of the template strand) where RNA polymerase binds to initiate transcription. It determines which strand will be used as template and the direction of transcription. The Terminator (D) is a sequence located downstream at the 3' end of the coding strand that signals the end of transcription. When RNA polymerase reaches the terminator, transcription stops and the newly synthesised RNA molecule is released. Both are crucial structural and regulatory elements of the transcription unit.

sub_questions.text: (d) अनुलेखन एकल (इकाई) में (C) तथा (D) की अवस्थिति का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (d) Describe the location of (C) and (D) in the transcription unit.

key_points: C (Promoter) is located upstream of the structural gene at the 3' end of the template strand
D (Terminator) is located downstream of the structural gene at the 3' end of the coding strand

sub_questions.solution: In the transcription unit, C (Promoter) is located upstream of the structural gene, at the 3' end of the template strand (or 5' end of the coding strand). It precedes the coding sequence and is the site where RNA polymerase first binds. D (Terminator) is located downstream of the structural gene, at the 3' end of the coding strand (or 5' end of the template strand). It follows the structural gene sequence and marks the end of the transcription unit. Together, these two regulatory sequences flank the structural gene — the promoter at the beginning and the terminator at the end.

sub_questions.text: (A) (i) मानव शुक्रजनक नलिका की आरेखीय काट का वर्धित आरेख बनाइए तथा इसके निम्नलिखित भागों को नामांकित कीजिए: (a) शुक्रजनन करने वाली कोशिकाएँ, (b) नरयुग्मक का पोषण करने वाली कोशिकाएँ, (c) वे कोशिकाएँ जिनमें प्रथम अर्धसूत्री विभाजन तथा द्वितीय अर्धसूत्री विभाजन होता है। (ii) शुक्राणु प्लाज्मा क्या है? शुक्राणु प्लाज्मा के दो संघटकों के नाम लिखिए। यह वीर्य (सीमेन) से किस प्रकार भिन्न है?
sub_questions.text_english: (A) (i) Draw a diagrammatic sectional view of human seminiferous tubule (enlarged) and label the following: (a) cell that undergoes spermiogenesis, (b) cell that nourish male gametes, (c) cell which undergoes meiosis I and meiosis II. (ii) State what is seminal plasma. Mention two constituents of seminal plasma. How is it different from semen?

key_points: (i)(a) Spermatid undergoes spermiogenesis; (b) Sertoli cells nourish male gametes; (c) Primary spermatocyte undergoes meiosis I, secondary spermatocyte undergoes meiosis II
(ii) Seminal plasma is the fluid component of semen secreted by accessory glands; constituents include fructose and prostaglandins; Semen = sperms + seminal plasma

sub_questions.solution:
(i) A seminiferous tubule (enlarged, sectional view) shows: (a) Spermatid – the cell that undergoes spermiogenesis (transformation of spermatid into mature spermatozoon); (b) Sertoli cells – the large, columnar cells that nourish and support the developing male gametes by providing nutrients; (c) Primary spermatocyte – the cell that undergoes meiosis I (to form secondary spermatocytes), and Secondary spermatocyte – the cell that undergoes meiosis II (to form spermatids). Spermatogonia (at the periphery) give rise to primary spermatocytes by mitosis.

(ii) Seminal plasma is the fluid portion of semen secreted by the accessory reproductive glands: seminal vesicles, prostate gland, and Cowper's glands (bulbourethral glands). Two major constituents of seminal plasma are fructose (which provides energy to spermatozoa) and prostaglandins (which aid in sperm transport). Seminal plasma differs from semen in that semen is the complete secretion containing both spermatozoa and the seminal plasma, whereas seminal plasma is only the acellular fluid component devoid of sperms.

sub_questions.text: (B) (i) उस परिघटना का उल्लेख कीजिए जो मानव में द्वितीयक अंडक को अर्धसूत्री विभाजन पूर्ण करने हेतु प्रेरित करता है। (ii) युग्मनज का गर्भाशय में अंतरोपण होने तक के पथ का निर्धारण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (B) (i) Mention the event that induces the completion of the meiotic division of the secondary oocyte in humans. (ii) Trace the journey of the zygote until its implantation inside the uterus.

key_points: (i) Fertilisation of the secondary oocyte by a sperm induces completion of meiosis II
(ii) Zygote → cleavage → 2-cell, 4-cell, 8-cell stages → morula → blastocyst → implantation in uterine endometrium

sub_questions.solution:
(i) In humans, the secondary oocyte is arrested at metaphase II of meiosis. The event that induces completion of meiosis II is fertilisation — specifically, the entry of the sperm into the secondary oocyte. Upon sperm penetration, the secondary oocyte is triggered to complete meiosis II, releasing the second polar body and forming the haploid ovum (egg nucleus), which then fuses with the sperm nucleus to form the diploid zygote.

(ii) The journey of the zygote to implantation: After fertilisation in the ampullary region of the fallopian tube, the zygote undergoes cleavage (mitotic divisions) while being transported towards the uterus. It successively passes through 2-cell, 4-cell, 8-cell, and 16-cell (morula) stages. The morula continues to divide and differentiates into a blastocyst, consisting of an outer layer of trophoblast cells and an inner cell mass (embryoblast). As the blastocyst moves along the fallopian tube and enters the uterus, the trophoblast cells attach to the endometrium (uterine lining) in a process called implantation, which occurs approximately 7-8 days after fertilisation.

sub_questions.text: (A) (i) माध्यम से पुनयोगज डीएनए को स्वीकार करने हेतु जीवाणु (बैक्टीरियल) कोशिका को 'सक्षम' कैसे बनाया जाता है? व्याख्या कीजिए। (ii) पीसीआर तकनीक का उपयोग करते हुए लाभकारी जीन के प्रवर्धन के विभिन्न चरणों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (A) (i) Explain how is a bacterial cell made 'competent' to take up recombinant DNA from the medium. (ii) Explain the steps of amplification of gene of interest using PCR technique.

key_points: (i) Competent cells made by treatment with divalent cations (CaCl2) to increase permeability of cell membrane; or by electroporation
(ii) PCR steps: Denaturation (94°C) → Annealing of primers → Extension by Taq polymerase (72°C); repeated multiple cycles

sub_questions.solution:
(i) A bacterial cell is normally not able to take up DNA from its environment because its cell membrane is not freely permeable to large molecules like DNA. To make it 'competent' (capable of taking up foreign DNA), the bacterial cells (typically E. coli) are treated with a divalent cation solution such as calcium chloride (CaCl₂) at ice-cold temperature (0°C). This treatment increases the permeability of the bacterial cell membrane. The recombinant DNA is then mixed with these competent cells and subjected to heat shock at 42°C for a short period. This heat shock further increases the uptake of DNA. Alternatively, electroporation (using brief electric pulses) can be used to create temporary pores in the membrane for DNA entry.

(ii) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) amplifies a specific gene using three steps repeated over 30-35 cycles. Step 1 – Denaturation: The double-stranded DNA is heated to about 94°C to separate the two strands. Step 2 – Annealing: The temperature is lowered to 50-65°C, allowing two specific primers (short synthetic oligonucleotides complementary to the flanking sequences of the gene of interest) to anneal to the respective complementary strands. Step 3 – Extension: The temperature is raised to 72°C, and a thermostable Taq DNA polymerase extends the primers using free deoxyribonucleotides and synthesises new DNA strands complementary to the template. Each cycle doubles the amount of DNA, resulting in exponential (2ⁿ) amplification of the target sequence.

sub_questions.text: (B) (i) पारजीवी (ट्रांसजेनिक) जन्तु क्या हैं? (ii) इन जन्तुओं का निर्माण क्यों किया जाता है? किन्हीं चार कारणों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (B) (i) What are transgenic animals? (ii) Why are these animals being produced? Explain any four reasons.

key_points: (i) Animals whose DNA has been manipulated to express an extra (foreign) gene are called transgenic animals
(ii) Reasons: study of gene regulation; biological products (insulin, vaccines); safety testing of drugs; study of disease models; improving animal productivity

sub_questions.solution:
(i) Transgenic animals are animals whose DNA has been altered by introducing a foreign gene (transgene) using recombinant DNA technology. They carry and express an extra gene in all their cells (or specific tissues). Examples include transgenic mice, rats, rabbits, pigs, sheep, and cows.

(ii) Transgenic animals are produced for the following reasons:

First, to study gene expression and regulation: transgenic animals help scientists understand how specific genes are switched on and off during development and in different tissues, aiding in understanding gene function in a whole organism.

Second, as biological factories for useful products: transgenic animals can be engineered to produce valuable biological substances in their milk, blood, or urine. For example, transgenic cows produce human alpha-lactalbumin-enriched milk, and transgenic sheep produce human AAT protein (alpha-1-antitrypsin) used to treat emphysema.

Third, for vaccine safety testing and drug toxicity testing: transgenic mice are used as animal models to test the safety and efficacy of new vaccines and drugs before human trials, replacing large numbers of traditional experimental animals.

Fourth, as disease models: transgenic animals that carry human disease genes are used as models for studying diseases like cancer, Alzheimer's, rheumatoid arthritis, and cystic fibrosis, helping to understand disease mechanisms and develop therapies.

sub_questions.text_english: (A) (i) Explain giving three reasons why tropics show greatest levels of species diversity. (ii) Draw a graph showing species-area relationship. Name the naturalist who studied such relationship. Write the observation made by him.

key_points: Reason 1: Tropics receive more solar energy, leading to higher productivity and more species
Reason 2: Tropical environments are less seasonal and more stable/predictable, allowing more niche specialisation
Reason 3: Tropics have not suffered the effects of glaciation and have had more evolutionary time for species diversification
Species-area relationship: log S = log C + Z log A (Alexander von Humboldt studied this); observation: species richness increases with area

sub_questions.solution:
(i) The tropics harbour the greatest species diversity for three major reasons. First, tropical regions receive abundant and consistent solar energy throughout the year, leading to high primary productivity. This greater energy availability supports more species and complex food webs. Second, tropical environments are far less seasonal and more stable and predictable compared to temperate and polar regions. This environmental constancy allows greater niche specialisation and thus promotes higher species richness over evolutionary time. Third, the tropics have not experienced the devastating effects of glaciation (ice ages) that exterminated many species in temperate regions. The tropical regions have had a much longer uninterrupted evolutionary time, allowing species to diversify and accumulate over millions of years.

(ii) The species-area relationship shows that species richness (S) increases with the area (A) in a regular fashion. On a log-log scale, the relationship is linear: log S = log C + Z log A, where Z is the slope (regression coefficient) and C is the y-intercept. This relationship was studied by the naturalist Alexander von Humboldt during his explorations of South American jungles. His observation was that within a region, species richness increases with increasing explored area, but only up to a limit. The value of Z (slope) typically ranges from 0.1 to 0.2 for smaller areas within a continent, but is much steeper (0.6-1.2) when comparing species richness across continents (inter-continental scale).

sub_questions.text_english: (B) (i) The world is facing the accelerated rate of species extinctions due to human activities. Explain any three major causes of biodiversity losses. (ii) Describe 'Ex situ' approach for conserving biodiversity. Give any two examples.

key_points: Causes: habitat loss and fragmentation; over-exploitation of species; alien species invasion; co-extinctions
Ex situ conservation: conserving threatened species outside their natural habitats
Examples: Zoological parks (zoos), botanical gardens, wildlife safari parks, seed banks, cryopreservation

sub_questions.solution:
(i) Three major causes of biodiversity losses due to human activities are:

First, habitat loss and fragmentation: This is the single biggest cause of biodiversity loss. Deforestation for agriculture, urbanisation, and industrialisation destroys natural habitats. When habitats are fragmented into smaller patches, populations become isolated, reducing gene flow and increasing vulnerability to local extinction.

Second, over-exploitation of species: Humans have over-harvested many species for food, medicine, timber, and trade. Commercial poaching of elephants for ivory, rhinoceroses for horns, and excessive fishing have pushed many species to the brink of extinction.

Third, introduction of alien (invasive) species: When exotic species are introduced (deliberately or accidentally) into new habitats, they may outcompete native species for resources, prey upon them, or introduce new diseases. For example, the Nile perch introduced into Lake Victoria in Africa led to the extinction of many native cichlid fish species.

(ii) Ex situ conservation refers to the conservation of threatened and endangered species outside their natural habitats in controlled conditions. This approach is used when in situ (in-habitat) conservation is insufficient or impractical. Two examples of ex situ conservation are: (1) Zoological parks (zoos) and wildlife safari parks, where animals are bred in captivity under protected conditions to maintain viable populations. (2) Seed banks (such as the Svalbard Global Seed Vault), where seeds of rare and threatened plant species are stored at low temperatures for long-term preservation and future restoration.
